condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Human amitriptyline oral bioavailability values of 40-60% (C04), 46±48% (C07), 48±11% (C12), 47.7±11.0% (C19), and 30-60% (C26) show that a lipophilic tricyclic tertiary amine with a basic side chain can exceed the 20% F threshold; the rat value of 4.4% (C29) is species-specific and does not override the consistent human data.

Human alfentanil oral bioavailability values of 37% (C01), 0.45±0.09 (C11), 0.42±0.15 (C18), and 41% (C28) support moderate oral bioavailability for the query's anilino-basic-amine scaffold; the single 1% table value (C13) is an outlier within that context.

L4 records show that structurally similar lipophilic basic amines are well absorbed in humans: imipramine human Fa is essentially 100% (C43, C48, C49, C53), amitriptyline HCl is freely soluble in water (C45), orphenadrine has a human FA of 95% (C52), and chloroquine is highly absorbed despite being a dicationic basic drug (C44). This directly supports the absorption component of F>=20%.

L5 gut-wall records show high permeability and no net efflux for close analogs: imipramine Caco-2 Papp A-B ~10.8×10^-6 cm/s with efflux ratio ~1.1 (C58, C62, C63, C66), desipramine high absorption 95-100% (C60), amitriptyline high rat intestinal permeability (C56), metoclopramide high adsorptive permeability (C59), tetrahydropalmatine high permeability (C65), and SB939 high permeability with low efflux (C57). Imipramine P-gp substrate status (C61, C64) does not translate into net efflux because the efflux ratio remains near 1.

Low-F records for selegiline (C02, C03, C06, C08, C09, C14, C16, C23), rotigotine/N-0437 (C10, C17, C25, C27), and brexanolone (C20) depend on specific liabilities—propargyl/MAO metabolism, phenolic conjugation/GI mucosal metabolism, and steroid scaffold—that are absent in the query, so they do not affirmatively establish F<20% for the query.
